explanation: Egyptians mummified cats in huge numbers as offerings. In 1890 one shipment of cat mummies was sold in England to be used as fertilizer.

claims.text: The goddess Bastet was usually depicted as a cat or as a woman with a cat's head.
Falcon, jackal and crocodile heads belong to other Egyptian gods, among them Horus, Anubis and Sobek.
Ancient Egyptians mummified very large numbers of cats as offerings.
In 1890 a shipment of ancient Egyptian cat mummies was sold in England for use as fertilizer.

results.title: The Case of the Cat Mummies That Became Fertilizer

evidence.summaryExcerpt: A 2023 journal article says about 180,000 mummified cats, weighing roughly 19.5 tons, were sent from Alexandria to Liverpool in February 1890 and auctioned as fertiliser. Liverpool Museums dates the auction to 10 February 1890, and a 10 February 1890 "Odd this day" post makes the same date claim.

claimResults.note: The year is supported by a 2023 journal article and by Liverpool Museums, which dates the Liverpool auction to 10 February 1890. Sources disagree on how many auctions there were and on prices, but not on the year, and the claim states neither.

issues.note: 'Usually shown as which animal, or with its head' reads awkwardly aloud. Early images show Bastet as a lioness, so 'usually' does real work, but a cat is still the one defensible option.

editor.reason: Both checks pass. High-risk c4 (1890) has web evidence in check B, whose summary attributes the year to a 2023 journal article and to Liverpool Museums. B's note on reading the stem aloud is fair, but the stem is clear, so it stays.
